findings.title: GOARCH=386 go vet fails to compile due to int overflow in untyped constants
findings.claim: On 386, GOARCH=386 go vet . fails to compile the package because untyped constants overflow int in serialization/varint/marshal_ints.go:123,126; this issue predates the PR and was already broken before it.

findings.title: Stale comment on nil/empty and dim=0 fallthrough
findings.claim: The comment at marshal.go:1006 says nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path, but the new bound at marshal.go:998-1003 now rejects a non-nil empty payload with Dimensions>0 before reaching this point, so only nil data and dim=0 actually fall through.

findings.title: Comment wrongly claims every path below allocates
findings.claim: The comment at marshal.go:986-991 states every path below turns the payload into an allocation, but an array destination allocates nothing, as the test comment at marshal_vector_test.go:649 confirms.

findings.title: Comment omits bound's role preventing zero-filled short payload decode
findings.claim: The comment at marshal.go:986-991 leaves out the bound's second job of stopping a short payload from silently decoding as zeroes when elemSize = len/Dimensions = 0.

findings.title: Comment overstates similarity to unmarshalList's bounding
findings.claim: The comment's claim that unmarshalList does the same is only loosely true: unmarshalList bounds by len/4 and only on the slice path.

findings.title: 32-bit wraparound claim is unproven because package can't build on 386
findings.claim: The test's arithmetic for bits.UintSize=32 wrapping 2^29+1 and 2^30+1 to 8 and 4 is correct, but the package does not build on 386 (per the go vet failure), so no 32-bit target can actually run these test cases, leaving the claimed 32-bit coverage unproven.

findings.title: Comment overstates guarantee that nil SubType is safe
findings.claim: The comment at marshal.go:995-997 implies a nil SubType is always safe, but it is only safe at dim=0; with dim>0 and non-nil data, vectorElemMinSize(nil) calls nil.Type() at marshal.go:1126 and panics, and a nested VectorType{SubType: nil} also panics through isVectorVariableLengthType. The base code panicked on the same inputs, so only the comment is wrong.

findings.title: MaxInt32 saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize is untested
findings.claim: The math.MaxInt32 saturation return in vectorElemMinSize at marshal.go:1134-1135 is never exercised by any test.

findings.title: Non-NULL empty []byte{} payload with dim>0 erroring has no direct test
findings.claim: The behaviour change the PR headlines, a non-NULL []byte{} payload with dim>0 now erroring, has no direct test; only 2-byte payloads are tested.

findings.title: Flat variable-length vector over a short payload is only tested nested
findings.claim: A flat variable-length vector, for example vector<text,3> over a short payload, is only tested nested, not in the flat case.

findings.title: Unannounced output change in getCassandraLongType for vector element type names
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType is only called from frame.go:860 and helpers.go:72, both for vector element types, so the change reaches only types inside a vector including collections, tuples and UDTs nested there; for those, String() and Custom() now carry the type name while Type() and marshal/unmarshal dispatch are unchanged, and this change is unannounced.

findings.title: Duplicate condition check between bound block and fast-path block
findings.claim: marshal.go:998 and :1007 test the same info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil condition back to back; the fast-path block could move inside the bound block instead.

findings.title: makeDoubleVectorType and makeFloat32VectorType could be simplified to one-line calls
findings.claim: makeDoubleVectorType and makeFloat32VectorType at marshal_vector_test.go:35 and ~47 could become one-line calls to makeVectorType.

findings.title: PR body and commits carry Claude attribution against user guidance
findings.claim: The PR body ends with '🤖 Generated with Claude Code', and commits 0276a66 and 78891dd both carry Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) trailers, which the global CLAUDE.md forbids; older commits on the branch carrying the same trailer don't waive the rule.

findings.title: PR body links to issues/PRs that 404 in this repo
findings.claim: #1085, #1086, #1106, #1093 and issues/1091 all return 404 in dkropachev/tidepool; they exist in scylladb/gocql instead.

findings.title: PR body lists closed #1106 as deferred work
findings.claim: #1106 is closed in scylladb/gocql, but the PR body lists it as deferred work.

findings.title: PR body's '#1093 rejects dim < 1' claim doesn't hold for this repo
findings.claim: The PR body says 'Lands with #1093, which rejects dim < 1', but #1093 is a closed PR in scylladb/gocql and frame.go:861 at head still has no dim < 1 check, so the claim does not hold for this repository.

findings.title: Commit 0276a66 subject understates the change
findings.claim: The subject 'Bound vector dimensions against the payload' doesn't mention that a short or empty non-NULL payload now errors instead of decoding to zeroes, or that the bound's message replaces the fast path's 'expected N bytes' error; only the PR body documents this, not the commit body.

findings.title: Commit 78891dd subject understates the change
findings.claim: The subject understates the change: it also changes getCassandraLongType for every unknown type name inside a vector element, including nested collections, tuples and UDTs.

findings.title: Commits and change deviate from CONTRIBUTING.md style and godoc requirements
findings.claim: CONTRIBUTING.md asks for a capitalised subject and a 'Patch by …; reviewed by …' trailer, and for functional changes to be noted in godoc, but the commits follow the repo's actual lowercase fix(scope): style and the empty-payload behaviour change has no godoc note.

findings.title: Three vector element classifiers could silently diverge if only one is updated
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize, vectorFixedElemSize (:1147) and isVectorVariableLengthType (:1181) agree today, but the rule that a nested fixed vector occupies dims×elem bytes now lives only in vectorElemMinSize, so adding a type to one classifier and not the others would weaken the bound without any error; vectorElemMinSize also detects nesting with elemType.(VectorType) rather than asVectorType, so a custom-typed vector gets the weaker 1-byte floor.

findings.title: Duplicated vector type builder helpers
findings.claim: makeVectorType and makeNestedVectorType repeat existing builders makeDoubleVectorType, makeFloat32VectorType, and makeFloatVectorType in vector_bench_test.go; makeVectorType(elem, elemName, …) also takes two arguments that can disagree.

findings.title: wireVectorType helper name doesn't reflect its generic behavior
findings.claim: wireVectorType parses any custom class string through readTypeInfo and has nothing vector-specific; a name like readCustomTypeInfo would better describe what it does.

findings.title: Wrap/no-recovery rationale is duplicated across comments, commit body, and test docs
findings.claim: The wrap and 'nothing recovers on Scan's goroutine' explanation appears at marshal.go:986-991 and :995-997, in the 0276a66 commit body, and in the test doc comments at :582-586 and :933-936.

findings.title: Style mix: new t.Parallel() calls and inline-slice test diverge from table-style tests
findings.claim: The base file had no t.Parallel() calls and the PR adds 18; TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType (:937) ranges over an inline slice instead of the tests := table style used elsewhere.

findings.title: PR body's claim that every new test fails against pristine code is false
findings.claim: The PR body's claim that every new test fails against pristine marshal.go/helpers.go is not true: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads, TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType, and the two concrete or resolvable-type subtests of :872 all pass on base as intended; TestVectorElemMinSize (:797) calls the new function so the whole test package fails to compile on base, meaning no test can fail individually.

findings.title: NULL-with-negative-dimensions base failure doesn't match any PR-listed failure mode
findings.claim: The NULL-with-negative-dimensions case fails on base because base returns nil, which is not one of the four failure modes the PR's validation claim lists.

findings.title: Undocumented behaviour change: NULL with negative dimensions now errors instead of…
findings.claim: On base, a NULL value with negative dimensions returned nil and left the destination untouched; head now returns a 'negative dimensions' error, but the PR's Behaviour change section only covers non-NULL payloads.

findings.title: Undocumented change: short payload to unsupported destination now gets bound error…
findings.claim: The bound now runs before the destination-type checks, so a short payload sent to an unsupported destination now gets the bound's error instead of 'Accepted types: …'; on a short payload, the destination is no longer overwritten with zeroes and the call instead returns an error and leaves it as it was.
